injuries.name: Gui Santos
injuries.detail: Santos exited Friday's game against the Trail Blazers with a knee injury in the second half and won't return.

injuries.name: Stephen Curry
injuries.detail: Curry (abdomen/oblique) has been ruled out for each of the Warriors' next three games, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports

injuries.name: Kristaps Porzingis
injuries.detail: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.

injuries.name: Moses Moody
injuries.detail: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.

injuries.name: Jimmy Butler III
injuries.detail: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.

injuries.name: Yanic Konan Niederhauser
injuries.detail: Niederhauser suffered a right toe injury during Friday's game against the Pelicans and won't return, Joey Linn of SI.com reports.

injuries.name: Bradley Beal
injuries.detail: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.

injuries.name: Jordan Miller
injuries.detail: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.

reasoning: On the season so far the Warriors are the stronger team; with home court the Warriors start about 2 points better, in a game of about 223 points.
Rest, travel and who is missing barely change it.
The mental side leans about 1 point towards the Clippers (revenge).
Bottom line: the Warriors win 54 times in 100, by about 1; most games like this end between 195 and 244 total points.
